description: Clicking "Télécharger PDF" on a resume's Preview page downloads a PDF file, with no browser print dialog. The PDF is generated on the server and is the same document the Preview shows and prints today.

userStories.title: The server returns the resume PDF the Preview shows
userStories.description: As a signed-in user, I want the server to produce my resume's PDF, so that a file can be downloaded without printing.
acceptanceCriteria: A new route returns `application/pdf` with `Content-Disposition: attachment` for a resume the signed-in user owns.
It returns 401 without a session, and 404 for a resume that does not exist or belongs to another user. Both are tested with two real users.

For each of the five templates, at a default and a non-default layout, the route's PDF matches the PDF printed from the Preview page under print media: same page count; same text, page by page; same page size (A4). The Modern band reaches the bottom of every page, as `e2e/modern-print-sidebar-full-page.spec.ts` checks.

When the client sends the unsaved draft and the photo, the PDF shows the draft's content and the photo exactly as the Preview does. Without them, it shows the stored resume and no photo. The draft is accepted only for the resume id in the URL; the photo is bounded as `boundedPhoto()` does.

Anything the client sends is treated as untrusted: rich text is sanitized as the Preview sanitizes it, and oversized payloads are rejected with 413. The renderer cannot be made to load an external URL or a local file. Tested with a malicious draft (script, iframe, remote image, `file://`).
The filename comes from the resume title, safely encoded: non-ASCII titles are RFC 5987-encoded, quotes are neutralized, and an empty title gives `resume.pdf`.
No print chrome: no browser header or footer, no date and no URL on any page.
FR-1: The PDF is produced by Chromium from the same template rendering and the same print stylesheet as the Preview. The new route renders no second, parallel layout of the CV.

FR-2: The layout comes from the account through `resolveResumeLayout`, as for the DOCX. The content is the stored resume, or the client-sent draft for the same resume id. The photo is the client-sent photo, bounded as for the DOCX.
FR-3: Authentication and ownership are enforced on the server. A client-sent draft never changes which resume is rendered or who owns it, and nothing it contains is persisted.

FR-4: The renderer runs with JavaScript limited to what the page needs. Network access is limited to the app's own origin, or the page is fully self-contained. Generation has a hard timeout, and the browser is always closed, even on error.
FR-5: No secret or session token reaches the rendered page, a log or an error response.
FR-6: All new user-facing strings live in `src/locales/{fr,en,de,it}/common.json`.
Regression constraint: The DOCX of every template is byte-identical (hashes of `word/document.xml` and `styles.xml`), and `git diff -- "src/app/api/resumes/[id]/download-docx"` is empty.

Regression constraint: Browser printing of the Preview page (Ctrl+P) produces the same PDF as before. The existing print e2e specs pass unchanged: `resume-print-geometry`; `modern-long-sidebar-print`; `modern-print-sidebar-full-page`; `resume-page-break-pdf-count`; the page-break specs.
Regression constraint: `pnpm test:visual` passes with its existing baselines; `pnpm test:parity` keeps every row's verdict (MATCH 211 / KNOWN 3 / NEW 0 on the current base).
Regression constraint: The Preview page renders, behaves and is captured exactly as today, apart from the PDF button's own states.
Regression constraint: The CSP and security headers keep passing `e2e/security-headers.spec.ts`. Any change to them is explicit and reviewed.
Verification: The CLAUDE.md §14 baseline on the final diff, lint judged against the ceiling of 306. Plus `pnpm test:visual` and `pnpm test:parity`.
Verification: Route tests: 401; 404 for another user's resume, with two real users; 413 for an oversized payload; content type, disposition and filename encoding.

Verification: Security tests: the malicious-draft cases (script, iframe, remote image, `file://`, an oversized photo). No external request and no file access occurs, shown by request interception or logs. `security-review` validation is required.
Verification: Fidelity, for all five templates at a default and a non-default layout: route PDF vs Preview print PDF: page count, text per page, page size; the Modern band check.
Verification: E2e for US-002: the click downloads a PDF; `window.print` is not called; busy and error states; a draft and a photo included.
Verification: DOCX: hashes before and after.
Verification: Vercel preview deployment (US-003): a manual run, recorded with status, time and page count. Deploying to the preview environment happens through the PR, not through a `vercel` command.
Verification: ui-expert: reviews the button's busy and error states (desktop and mobile), and the downloaded PDF opened in a viewer.
FAIL condition: The print dialog opens, or `window.print()` is called, when "Télécharger PDF" is clicked.
FAIL condition: For any template, the downloaded PDF differs from the Preview's print in page count, page text or page size, or loses the Modern band.
FAIL condition: The draft or the photo the user sees in the Preview is missing from the PDF when present.
FAIL condition: Any user can obtain another user's resume PDF, or the route answers without a session.
FAIL condition: The renderer fetches an external URL or a local file, or runs script supplied by the client.
FAIL condition: Any DOCX byte changes, any visual baseline needs updating, or parity reports NEW > 0 or a changed verdict.
FAIL condition: A user-facing string is hardcoded or missing in a locale.
BLOCKER condition: The headless-browser dependency cannot run within the Vercel plan's limits (function size, memory, duration). Report the measured numbers to the owner before any workaround.
BLOCKER condition: The PR's Vercel preview deployment cannot be exercised, for example because a protected deployment needs the owner's access. US-003 then waits for the owner.
BLOCKER condition: Fidelity with the Preview would require changing the templates or the print stylesheet, which is out of scope.

Out of scope: The Word / DOCX export, in any way (owner constraint carried over from `modern-print-sidebar-full-page`): no change under `src/app/api/resumes/[id]/download-docx/`, and no DOCX byte change.
Out of scope: Cover-letter PDFs (`html2pdf.js` / `jspdf`), which are a separate surface.
Out of scope: The dashboard card's "Download PDF" stub.
Out of scope: Storing the photo or the draft on the account.
Out of scope: Changing the print stylesheet, the templates or the page geometry. Browser printing (Ctrl+P) keeps working as today.
Out of scope: Deploying to production. Deployment stays an owner shipping action; this PRD only requires the change to work on the PR's Vercel preview deployment.

userStories.title: PDF generation works in the production runtime
